A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CONSIGN and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Inspection of all 18 pages in each version supports comparison, including matching relocated experiments and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments across five datasets, including uncertainty-volume estimates, sampled coverage, correlations, qualitative predictions, calibration values, and computational timings.

after.justification: v2 retains original CONSIGN experiments and reports revised results and additional RAPS/SACP comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: CONSIGN retains the same SVD construction, coefficient bounds, argmax projection, label-wise tolerance, and numerical calibration procedure. Equations (4)–(11) and Algorithms 1–2 remain substantively unchanged; the revised comparison methods do not modify CONSIGN.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate M&Ms-2, MS-CMR19, LIDC, COCO-animals, and COCO-vehicles with the same segmentation domains and class coverage. The MS-CMR19 accuracy settings exchange main-text and appendix placement; neither setting is newly added.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates APS as its sole comparator. v2 replaces it with regularized APS (RAPS) and adds Liu et al.'s neighborhood-aggregation SACP throughout the quantitative and qualitative comparisons. This evaluated SACP is distinct from Bereska et al.'s similarly named work already cited in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the reported cardiac U-Net dropout from 0.5 to 0.4 and the MS-CMR19 test count from 173 to 98, retaining 500 calibration images. The new baselines introduce regularization and neighborhood-aggregation settings, including different SACP weights in main and appendix experiments. Metrics and the overall calibration/test design remain stable; these disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 5 and 9 extend the qualitative spatial-consistency comparisons to SACP and revise some cardiac and lung examples. The existing comparisons across principal-component counts, sample sizes, and accuracy settings remain. No new systematic ablation or distribution-shift test is presented.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random calibration/test splits, error bars representing ±1 standard deviation, and fold-specific calibration values. The added SACP results follow this existing reporting practice; no new seed information or statistical testing procedure appears.

E6.justification: v2 adds SACP results throughout Figures 2–9 and new Table 5, reporting behavior broadly similar to RAPS. Existing CONSIGN calibration values also change: Table 3's COCO-vehicles result at (α, β, K) = (0.3, 0.75, 2), Fold 1, changes from 0.710 to 0.330. These substantial additions and revisions are not clean evidence of same-setting performance gains because comparator and experimental settings also change.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, its exchangeability and finite-termination conditions, and Appendix A's proof are unchanged. v2 adds mathematical definitions for RAPS/SACP and strengthens the truncated-PCA argument from obtaining a reasonably large prediction set to asserting that it always includes the ground truth. No corresponding proof supports that stronger inclusion assertion.

C1.justification: The central claims remain spatially correlated prediction sets with user-specified statistical guarantees, compatibility with sampling-capable segmentation models, and improved uncertainty estimates. v2 expands the supporting comparisons and emphasizes the low-rank, discrete-projection contribution already explained in v1 Section 3.2.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation attributing SACP's similarity to pixel-wise methods to score aggregation duplicating effects of model training, and attributes worse repeated aggregation to oversmoothing. It strengthens the interpretation of truncated PCA and removes v1's limitation concerning the essentially linear SVD representation. Exchangeability and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset access links, specifies the first-900-MRI selection and use of nonzero-ground-truth MRIs, and documents RAPS/SACP hyperparameters and one aggregation iteration. The PDFs do not establish that the newly disclosed MRI restrictions were newly applied. Hardware, core optimizer settings, and existing pretrained-model code links remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for PhiSeg, Stochastic Segmentation Networks, Davenport's conformal segmentation work, and Liu et al.'s SACP, while removing two conformal-prediction references. It clarifies positioning against existing PCA-based restoration methods. The Angelopoulos conference/preprint citation change refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The separate Conformal Prediction section is incorporated into the Introduction, experiments receive numbered subsections, and Appendix B is subdivided. Abstract, motivation, PCA explanation, and conclusion passages are edited, while most method, metric, and proof exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The result presentation is extensively revised: six quantitative figures incorporate the new comparator series and revised legends, Figures 5 and 9 expand their qualitative comparison grids, and Table 5 is added. Figure 1 moves, captions gain metric interpretations, and appendix plots and examples are substantially repacked.

improvement.justification: Replacing the APS-only comparison with RAPS and an evaluated spatial comparator makes the central spatial-dependence claim more convincingly tested. Added baseline settings and dataset details also improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by v2's unsupported assertion that truncated PCA always includes the ground truth and removal of the linearity limitation; the formal guarantee and proof themselves remain unchanged.
